metadata.title: A Day to Weekly Market
metadata.description:
Click to tweet and share this recipe: http://ctt.ec/rj27T

Once a week people from scores of tiny villages located in thick forests of Garo hills and the West Khasi hills descend down to the plains in Assam border to stock up food supplies, medicine and general shopping for the week. 

Market days are special days here in these remote villages and it happens on every Tuesday. They are so big an affair that even schools don't function on a market day. 

Garo and Khasi villagers climb down the mountains to a location from where they get vehicles and go to the market, usually 10 - 15 Kms away from our villages. Some even trek the entire distance on foot. 

In this video I trek to a Khasi market located in a place called Langphi in the East Khasi hills. While going we trek to a place from where we took a vehicle and while coming back we trekked our way back 20 kilometers, throught a forest which is known to have bears and is a tiger corridor. 

One of my uncle is a traditional healer and needed bark of a particular tree, whose wood looks like flesh and when you cut it blood like sap oozes out of it. On our way back we had to do quite a bit of searching for this elusive tree.

Tired to the core, we reached home just before sunset and were so happy to find the dogs waiting for us at home, which went missing trying to follow us in a far off place.
